'I heard screaming': neighbourhood party 'crashed' by alleged attackers

The group dispersed before police arrived.

Actual Article Body:

Witnesses say almost a dozen police cars swarmed a "quiet" cul-de-sac in Belconnen after violence erupted at a neighbourhood party at the weekend.

Login or signup to continue reading

The Canberra Times spoke to multiple residents in the area after the incident on Saturday, November 14.

A witness said a large group of young people gatecrashed a private gathering in Flynn and "bashed" multiple people, including adults, when they were refused entry.

"It was horrific ... I'm scared for myself," the witness said, adding that there were at least 20 teenagers brawling on Brodie Place about 9pm.

She said the alleged attackers were known for "ruining" parties in Belconnen.

"There was [property damage], pots being thrown. By the time police came, it was too late," she said.

"Multiple people were calling 000."

A nearby resident said he didn't see what occurred but heard the celebration being interrupted by people yelling and screaming at one another.

During the incident, he checked in on a next-door neighbour who said theirs was a quiet and peaceful area.

Another resident said this was the first time such an incident had occurred in the area.

"I heard a lot of screaming. But it was very dark ... we don't have many streetlights here, apart from one," the man said.

"I just saw kids running up and down. There was a fight. I could see young guys taking off their shirts so they could come and get into it because that's what intelligent people do, apparently," he said.

After the incident, the resident said he saw flashing lights and about 10 police cars came to the neighbourhood.

ACT Policing is investigating the incident reported about 9.45pm on Saturday, November 14.

A police spokeswoman said police received multiple calls regarding an altercation involving a large group of people on Brodie Place in Flynn.

"When police arrived, the group had dispersed and the alleged assailants could not be located," the spokeswoman said.

An ACT Emergency Services spokeswoman said no ambulances were called to the incident on November 14. Police are urging witnesses and people with footage of the altercation to contact Crime Stoppers ACT quoting reference number 8557043.
